name: First Polotsk
summary: Wittgenstein followed Oudinot back to Polotsk on the Dvina and attacked. On the 17th the Russians pressed the French and Bavarians back to the town, and Oudinot was wounded. Saint-Cyr, taking over, struck back without warning in the afternoon of the 18th, his Bavarians and French columns breaking the Russian line and taking guns, though Deroy was mortally wounded; Wittgenstein fell back, and Saint-Cyr won his marshal's baton.

forces.name: Legrand's Division
forces.summary: Held the line before Polotsk on the 17th, and on the 18th led the French part of Saint-Cyr's counter-attack.
notes: After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812.
Each regiment had its own two or four 3-pdrs, shown as Regimental Artillery.
The horse battery, without the three cavalry regiments the list wants for it, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Verdier's Division
forces.summary: Fought in the centre on the 17th, where Verdier was wounded; Maison took over the division.
notes: After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812.
Each regiment had its own two or four 3-pdrs, shown as Regimental Artillery.
Pouget's brigade mixes a regimental battery with a section, and the horse battery has none of the three cavalry regiments the list wants for it; both show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Merle's Division
forces.summary: Merle's Swiss and Croatians held the left of the line by the Dvina on both days.
notes: After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812.
Each regiment had its own two or four 3-pdrs, shown as Regimental Artillery.
The Swiss regiments and the Croatians are shown as Line.
The horse battery, without the three cavalry regiments the list wants for it, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Corbineau's and Doumerc's Cavalry
forces.formation: II Corps cavalry and 3rd Cuirassier Division
forces.summary: Out on the flanks; on the 18th Doumerc's cuirassiers rode down the Russian cavalry that had taken a Bavarian battery.
notes: After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812. The light regiments were down to two to four hundred men each, so they are Small, as is the 7th Cuirassiers.
Doumerc's three brigades of one regiment each are shown together.
Cavalry without infantry, two light brigades and the second horse battery show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Deroy's Division
forces.summary: Saint-Cyr's right wing, which opened the surprise attack on the 18th and drove deep into the Russian line; Deroy fell mortally wounded at its head.
notes: After Nafziger's returns of 29 August and 15 September 1812.
Typhus and the march had wrecked the Bavarian corps: Nafziger's returns give whole regiments three to five hundred men, so every battalion is Small.
The howitzer battery is left out.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Wrede's Division
forces.summary: Beside Deroy's, it went in on the 18th and took the Russian batteries in the centre.
notes: After Nafziger's returns of 29 August and 15 September 1812.
Typhus and the march had wrecked the Bavarian corps: Nafziger's returns give whole regiments three to five hundred men, so every battalion is Small.
Two foot batteries where the list's divisional artillery takes one show as a historical departure.
The corps' four chevau-léger regiments were with the main army, not at Polotsk.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Helfreich's Advance Guard
forces.summary: Kulnev's old advance guard, under Helfreich since his death, which led the attack on the French positions before Polotsk on the 17th.
notes: After Nafziger's return of Wittgenstein's corps for 14 August.
No Infantry Brigade shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 1 of the 2 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Berg's First Line
forces.summary: The corps' first line, which pressed the French back towards Polotsk on the 17th and on the 18th was caught by Saint-Cyr's surprise counter-attack in the afternoon, losing guns before the cavalry and reserves restored the line.
notes: After Nafziger's return for 14 August. The 23rd Jäger is attached to the Kaluga regiment, as the list takes Jäger.
Three regiments in Sibirsky's brigade and two batteries in it, the converged Guard depot squadrons, and dragoons and cuirassiers mixed in one brigade, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

forces.name: Sazonov's Second Line
forces.summary: The 14th Division in the second line, fed in to hold the centre when Saint-Cyr's attack broke through on the 18th.
notes: After Nafziger's return for 14 August. The converged Jäger of the 11th's and 36th's reserve battalions are attached to the Navaginsk regiment.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.

regiments.name: Navaginsk Infantry with Converged (11th and 36th Reserve) Jäger

forces.name: Kakhovsky's Reserve
forces.summary: The corps' grenadiers and horse guns, which held the line while Wittgenstein drew off after the second day.
notes: After Nafziger's return for 14 August, which also gives two converged infantry regiments; they're left out.
Six reserve grenadier battalions in a brigade that takes two regiments, and two horse batteries with one dragoon regiment, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 2 of the 3 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.
